justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mild upward drift from what I assessed as a recent price level around $245–246 for the underlying asset, likely an equity index or ETF. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of $245.8 is essentially a near-flat carry from the prior close, acknowledging that short-term mean reversion tends to dominate and that there is no strong directional signal strong enough to justify a meaningful move in either direction over a single session. At the one-week horizon, I nudged the estimate slightly higher to $246.5, reflecting a modest positive drift assumption consistent with a slight equity risk premium over a short holding period. At the one-month horizon, the estimate of $248.0 continues that gentle upward trend, incorporating compounding of the drift while also acknowledging that broader macroeconomic momentum at the time of the forecast appeared modestly constructive.

The confidence interval widths expand significantly across horizons in a manner consistent with the square-root-of-time scaling typical of financial returns. At one day, the 90% interval spans roughly $10.6, implying a daily volatility in the range of 1–1.5%, which is fairly standard for a broad equity index. By one week, the interval widens to about $21, and by one month it reaches $40, reflecting the accumulation of uncertainty over longer periods. I calibrated these widths using historical realized volatility as a baseline, while also accounting for the elevated uncertainty in the macro environment at the time, including shifting interest rate expectations and geopolitical factors that can cause volatility clustering and fat-tailed return distributions.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, a surprise Federal Reserve communication signaling more aggressive tightening, a significant geopolitical escalation, or a sudden credit event in financial markets could produce a sharp selloff that breaks below even the lower one-month bound of $228. Liquidity dislocations, which tend to amplify moves, are particularly concerning at monthly horizons. On the upside, a surprisingly strong earnings season, a dovish pivot signal from central banks, or a rapid de-escalation of geopolitical tensions could push prices well above $268. My intervals are explicitly probabilistic and carry roughly a 10% combined probability of being breached, so tail outcomes are always plausible even under a relatively benign base case.
